title: Bound one tensor axis by two section errors (no new κ)
body:
## Question

#4487 bounds the scalar monomial `2g (10 p^2 + p^6 exp(-p^2))^{g-1} p^6 exp(-p^2)` and leaves open whether the tensor difference is at most that monomial. What does one axis of the product contribute?

## Result

Let `ε = p^6 exp(-p^2)`. If every axis satisfies `||B_i|| ≤ 10 p^2`, `||C_i|| ≤ 10 p^2 + ε` and `||B_i - C_i|| < 2 ε`, and if `||X ⊗ Y|| = ||X|| ||Y||`, then

```text
⊗_i B_i - ⊗_i C_i = sum_k T_k,
```

with `T_k` changing only axis `k`. Each slice has norm strictly less than `2 (10 p^2 + ε)^{g-1} ε`, and the sum of the slices is strictly less than `2g (10 p^2 + ε)^{g-1} ε`.

The factor 2 is the sum of two section errors on the active axis. The scalar check is the one-dimensional case: for caps `10`, `11` and `2`, the three slices add to the product difference, and a `g = 1` difference of `3` exceeds the cap.

**Claim type:** one telescoping bound. **No new κ.** The three axis inequalities stay hypotheses. The comparison with `2^{-C p}` is #4487 and is not re-proved. The #4100 notes are unchanged.

The locality audit already records this shape with `p^{10}` in place of `10 p^2` and `p^6`. This branch starts from canonical main. It does not replay #4487.
